assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base into another by deaminase chemistry on a single-stranded R-loop, without double-strand breaks or donor templates. This is a new, clearly defined molecular tool that connects nucleotide chemistry to genome stability and is already used in human therapy. Strongly aligned with a DNA-chemistry perspective.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader. Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, which required evolving a deaminase for DNA) were the lead trainees on the first two papers. Liu alone, or Liu with Komor and Gaudelli, is a coherent configuration. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were independent and near-simultaneous, which could complicate a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Introduced 2016-2017 and now clinically validated, including reports of treatment in patients. Independent confirmation and broad adoption are strong, so timing is reasonable though still fairly young.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed as base editing alone or together with prime editing (B041), which has the same lead laureate.
The weight to give the independent Target-AID work by Kondo and Nishida.
Long-term clinical safety is not fully established; I am relying on my recollection of the clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into inducers of ubiquitin-mediated degradation. PROTACs (heterobifunctional) and molecular glues (thalidomide analogs acting through cereblon) form a coherent mechanistic and chemical principle with large pharmaceutical impact, and I find the biochemical mechanism of E3 ligase hijacking compelling.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (Sakamoto was the first author of the 2001 paper with both). Ciulli contributed the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex mechanism. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which is a separate pillar and creates a crowded credit list of eight names. Crews, Deshaies and Handa or Ciulli is plausible; I chose the three I judge most decisive.
assessment.maturity: Many PROTACs are in clinical trials and the molecular glue lenalidomide is a long-established drug, but no PROTAC approval is, to my knowledge, final. Mechanistic confirmation is strong and the concept is stable.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTAC and molecular glue lines may need different recognition.
The correct split of credit between Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli and the cereblon discoverers.
Clinical outcomes of PROTACs are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators and clustered single molecules transformed biology and medicine, and rests on nucleotide chemistry and polymerase engineering. Its impact is immense and it directly concerns DNA polymerase substrates and nucleotide analogs.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry and platform and are the most natural pair. Mayer is credited for clustered amplification and the Manteia approach. Rothberg (pyrosequencing on beads) and Ju (terminator chemistry) are alternatives that make credit contested.
assessment.maturity: The technology is mature, ubiquitous and has been confirmed for two decades; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit is divided among competing platform inventors and patent histories.
Whether a chemistry committee would see this as chemistry or as a technology for biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics allows cell-wide measurement of proteins, modifications and turnover. The enabling methods include shotgun proteomics, stable isotope labeling and targeted approaches. I use the same LC-MS/MS techniques in my own field for nucleotide pool quantification, so I know their importance first hand.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most commonly cited leaders of the field, with distinct contributions (high-resolution workflows, quantitative and targeted proteomics, shotgun proteomics). Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, so the cut-off is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and confirmed. Mass spectrometry in chemistry has already been honoured (2002 for ESI and MALDI), so a committee may view this as an extension rather than a new principle.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize may lower urgency.
Number of deserving contributors exceeds three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled efficient in vivo delivery of siRNA and mRNA, making the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and RNA therapeutics possible. Chemically the discovery is the design of ionizable lipids with pKa tuned for endosomal escape. The medical impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Cullis is the leading figure for LNP formulation and ionizable lipid concepts, with Madden, Hope and MacLachlan as collaborators. Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipidoid libraries. Credit is spread across academia and companies, and 2023 Medicine recognition of nucleoside-modified mRNA covers a neighbouring part of the story.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale through vaccines and an approved siRNA drug (patisiran), so very mature, although the delivery technology is still being refined.
uncertainties: Attribution among six credited names is complicated by company histories and patents.
Whether the chemistry of lipid design is judged to be sufficiently distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation of RNA with writers, erasers and readers established epitranscriptomics as a regulatory layer in gene expression. It is an elegant case of nucleic acid chemical modification controlling biology, and is connected to metabolic and disease processes.
assessment.attribution: He proposed reversibility and identified FTO as an eraser. Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini and Meyer) mapped m6A transcriptome-wide in 2012. The assignment is plausible but contested between the mapping and the reversibility discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Active and rapidly expanding, with some disagreement over mechanisms, mapping accuracy and the roles of individual readers. Possibly premature relative to older candidates.
uncertainties: Debates over antibody specificity and quantitative stoichiometry in mapping methods.
Medical relevance is still largely preclinical.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion using orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs incorporates noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells. It is a general tool that links chemistry to translation fidelity and protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang created the first orthogonal pairs for eukaryotic and bacterial cells, and Chin extended to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama are valuable but fewer decisive contributions would be needed for a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and widely used; the technology continues to mature but is still more tool-driven than therapeutic.
uncertainties: Uncertain how to divide credit between the founders of the first pairs and later reprogramming work.
Whether the breadth of applications meets prize-level impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing allows electrical reading of single nucleic acid molecules, culminating in commercial long-read sequencing that also detects modified bases. This is a conceptually bold single-molecule approach with direct relevance to nucleotide chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Branton, Deamer and Kasianowicz proposed the basic idea, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled DNA translocation that made sequencing practical. The trio selected reflects what I consider the largest practical contributions, but the earlier conceptual roots are disputed.
assessment.maturity: Technology is now in routine use and has been independently validated, although accuracy and throughput continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Credit among five pioneers is difficult to allocate.
Competition with other sequencing technologies in terms of ultimate lasting impact.
